title: Trajectory-based prompt sampling for per-vertical quant calibration packs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Our current calibration packs for FP8/INT8 quantization are assembled from static reservoir/stratified samplers and miss trajectory/context signals present in production sessions. This causes underestimated errors on multi-turn flows where token distribution and attention patterns differ from isolated single-turn prompts. Goal: produce per-vertical calibration mini-packs that preserve session trajectories, context-window transitions, and rare-but-critical prompt sequences so quant profiles reflect real production behavior across verticals (search QA, chat assistants, summarization). Deliver a repeatable sampling recipe and tooling to generate these packs nightly from production logs while respecting privacy controls.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A reproducible sampler that outputs per-vertical calibration packs (target size 50k tokens per pack) preserving session trajectories and context-length distribution.
2) Validation harness that runs INT8 and FP8 quantized variants against FP16 baseline and reports per-domain metrics (token-error-rate, perplexity ratio, token-confidence-delta, embedding drift).
3) For three pilot verticals (commerce-chat, docs-summarize, billing-support) the accuracy drop metric (token-error-rate) must be <= 1.5% on INT8 and <= 0.8% on FP8 against baseline, or automatically flagged for review.
4) End-to-end pipeline runs nightly and artifacts (packs + manifest) are stored in S3 with versioned keys and manifest includes sampling seed and parameters.
5) Documentation and runbook completed and reviewed by PM + Applied ML.
tech_notes: Sampling algorithm high-level: 1) Ingest production request logs and group by session_id; discard sessions < 2 requests (configurable). 2) Segment sessions into trajectories by conversation turn boundaries and context-window overlap (sliding windows of 512/1024 tokens depending on vertical). 3) Bucket trajectories by context length, intent label (if available), and token-entropy estimate; sample proportional to traffic weight but apply a floor to rare buckets (min coverage). 4) Apply time-decay weighting to prefer recent behavior (half-life configurable; default 28 days) while retaining a headroom of older exemplars for long-tail stability. 5) Anchor sampling: seed each pack with top-K exemplars per vertical identified by high-variance calibration-sensitive features (high attention locality, long KV cache reuse). 6) Rarity upsampling: upweight sessions with low embedding-frequency clusters to preserve edge cases. 7) Privacy: PII scrub step (regex + model-assisted detection) and redact before storing. 8) Synthetic augmentation: where session length < desired context, stitch semantically-similar sessions from same vertical using policy constraints to avoid creating unrealistic turn boundaries. Implementation notes: use Spark job for nightly extraction, Rust sampler binary for deterministic pack generation (seeded), manifest JSON lines with metadata (seed, sampler version, vertical, time-range, counts).
validation_plan: 1) Offline validation: run quantized model variants on generated packs and compute metrics: token-error-rate (TER), perplexity ratio (quant/F16), top-1 logit flip rate, embedding cosine drift (avg and 95th percentile), and downstream decode-quality checks for structured outputs. 2) Statistical tests: use bootstrap on per-trajectory TER to compute 95% CI; require upper bound < threshold. 3) Cross-vertical sanity: compare distributional statistics (length, entropy, embedding clusters) between pack and recent production sample; flag KL divergence > 0.05. 4) Regression gating: if any pilot vertical exceeds thresholds, create a QA ticket for quant profile tuning and hold rollout. 5) A/B canary: deploy quantized model to 0.5% production traffic for each vertical with per-request logging of confidence shifts and planner-level fallbacks. 6) Post-deploy checks: 24h and 72h rolling checks; auto-rollback if metric delta exceeds SLO-defined limits.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal ML validation on packs (team-only). Phase 2: canary vs baseline on staging datasets. Phase 3: 0.5% production traffic per vertical with tight monitoring and automatic fallback to FP16 for routes with >1.0% error spike. Phase 4: 5% traffic observe 48h stability, then gradual increase to target (as per Dedicated/Hosted config). Document explicit rollback criteria and SLO thresholds in the runbook. Maintain a labeled artifact registry (s3://redwood-quant-calibration/{vertical}/{date}/manifest.json) and link versions to releases.
